summary: Major AI companies are making significant moves, with Databricks raising $5B and OpenAI introducing a new mode for its GPT-5.6 model. IBM is partnering with OpenAI to train consultants, while Anthropic is exploring AI safety concerns. Microsoft is simplifying its Copilot apps and Nvidia is planning to make its GPUs more valuable.
insight: The increasing focus on AI safety and regulation is driving innovation in the industry, with companies like OpenAI and Anthropic leading the charge.
highlights: OpenAI introduces Ultrafast mode for its GPT-5.6 model
IBM partners with OpenAI to train consultants on AI technologies

articles.title: Databricks wanted to raise $1B, investors wanted $15B. It settled on $5B at a $190B valuation.
articles.description: AI is expensive, Ali Ghodsi tells TechCrunch. With so many investors wanting into his latest round, he said yes to more than planned.

articles.title: OpenAI introduces ‘Ultrafast,’ a new mode that makes GPT-5.6 Sol work at 14x the speed
articles.description: OpenAI is launching a preview of a sped up version of its latest, most powerful model, in an effort to court enterprise users.

articles.title: IBM partners with OpenAI to bolster enterprise AI push
articles.description: IBM plans to train and certify tens of thousands of consultants on OpenAI's technologies as part of this deal.

articles.title: Anthropic set AI agents loose on the same task. They started a turf war.
articles.description: Anthropic researchers found AI agents can clash, collude, and coordinate in unexpected ways, raising new questions about whether today’s safety tests capture the risks of multi-age

articles.title: OpenAI hires new CRO as executive shake-up continues
articles.description: Dali Rajic will take over as OpenAI's top salesperson.

articles.title: Microsoft kills off unsuccessful AI features while merging its separate Copilot apps
articles.description: Microsoft is simplifying Copilot by combining its consumer and business apps, and dropping AI-generated podcasts, Group Chats, Deep Research, and its Mico character.

articles.title: Nvidia’s new $500B plan is risky but brilliant, especially for aging GPUs
articles.description: Nvidia has a plan to make sure its GPUs won't lose value. It wants to convince a new crop of financiers to keep lending for AI buildouts.

articles.title: Anthropic could be worth $2 trillion when it goes public
articles.description: Rapid revenue growth fuels hope Claude maker's IPO is the biggest listing in history

articles.title: Claude's new Scarlet Letter watermark is invisible—for now
articles.description: The mark flags anything Claude processed, even human writing it only edited.

articles.title: OpenAI appoints Dali Rajic as Chief Revenue Officer
articles.description: OpenAI appoints Dali Rajic as Chief Revenue Officer to lead its global revenue organization and help businesses realize the full value of AI.

articles.title: Some Claude users are mad that Anthropic’s new watermarks will catch them using it at their jobs, classes
articles.description: Is Anthropic's new watermarking system a travesty? Some have taken to social media to complain that it is.

articles.title: OpenAI-backed Thrive Holdings raises $2B to bring AI to the enterprise
articles.description: Thrive Holdings has raised $2 billion in new funding at a $12 billion valuation from investors like SoftBank, D1 Capital Partners, and Altimeter Capital.
